correctness.rationale: For any specified simple endpoint path, trees containing its edges are in bijection with spanning trees after contracting it; the cofactor at the contracted vertex is precisely the Laplacian principal minor on the vertices outside the path, with parallel edges counted. Different endpoint paths are mutually exclusive in a tree. An exact separate implementation evaluated the minors and exhaustively summed them for all 66 pairs (30, 30, 6 by distance). Every length entry matched, each row summed to the separately computed cofactor 5,184,000, and the rational means and geodesic masses matched. In particular 7/30 < 26/75 < 11/30 gives the asserted nonmonotonicity. The standard UST path/chronological loop-erasure identity applies to the unweighted walk stopped at the fixed endpoint.
residual_risks: The independently written checker uses the same justified contraction identity; it is not a second derivation of that identity. The census is for the unit-conductance graph only.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a canonical small regular polyhedral graph with exactly three pair distances. The complete distribution is a finite exact test case for UST or LERW length calculations at near, intermediate and antipodal separation. In particular it provides a concrete counterexample to monotone dependence of the geodesic probability on separation: an antipodal pair has more compulsory steps but also more short routes, and the exact comparison is not captured by the adjacent resistance or the total spanning-tree count.
residual_risks: This is a finite benchmark and witness; it is not a theorem about other polyhedra or a new determinant method.
